text:
Rhea: Following up from the All-hands pricing segment  thought it made sense to capture some of the more nuanced Qs here. Ill kick it off: are there hard daily caps for free-tier accounts or just monthly credit limits?
Paula: Free tier currently enforces a soft daily cap (to prevent abuse) in addition to the monthly credits. Soft caps throttle with 429s and show a banner in the Console. We periodically review the thresholds; theyre designed to let devs experiment but block sustained scraping.
Marco: Can we be explicit about the difference between rate limits (requests/sec) and quotas (monthly tokens)? Customers keep mixing them up in sales calls.
Nina: Short explainer we can put in the FAQ: rate limits are instantaneous/rate (requests or tokens per second) enforced per-key; quotas are longer-term allowances (daily/monthly tokens or compute units) enforced per-account.
Rhea: Whats the policy for applying early-bird promo credits to accounts that already used some tokens during trial?
Paula: Promo credits are applied on top of existing usage going forward. If the promo is retroactive we show a credit line on the next invoice; otherwise the promo covers future consumption until its exhausted or expires. All promo T&Cs are shown on the Billing > Credits page.
Marco: A product ask: can we surface an "estimated burn" graph that projects end-of-month credit usage based on trailing 7 days? Sales teams requested it to help customers avoid surprise overages.
Nina: We have a prototype in DevEx. It uses daily token burn and a simple linear projection; we plan to add a confidence band and an option to project using a rolling-window percentile (e.g., 95th).
OpsBot: System notice: example alert rule uploaded to Console > Alerts: "Credits burn > 75% projection". Link: https://internal.redwood/alerts/templates/credits-burn
Rhea: Good. Also, in cases where customers hit unexpected overage due to platform issues (e.g., routing duplications), what's our remediation playbook?
Paula: We credit or refund at our discretion after investigation. The playbook: 1) customer raises ticket with X-Request-Id(s), 2) we validate duplication/bug in logs, 3) apply credit and follow-up. Well publish the runbook and an "appeal" link in Billing > Help.
Marco: Any change to how bursts are billed? Need to confirm: bursts are charged as normal usage, but do we meter them separately for reporting?
Paula: Bursts are normal usage in the meter; in the Console we flag burst-originated requests in the usage report so teams can filter them. No separate billing line item, but the UI exposes a "burst events" filter.
Nina: Action items: Paula to write the Billing playbook snippet and promo T&C clarifier, Marco to add the burn-projection mock to the product board, and DevEx (me) to wire the alert template into the demo workspace.
Rhea: Thanks — can we reconvene briefly once the Billing doc is drafted? Id like a one-pager for sales and customer success.
Paula: Will do. ETA 4 business days for a draft.
Rhea: Great. Closing this thread once the draft is linked. :rocket:
